requirements.requirement: Serve HTTPS on port 8443 with a certificate on node1
requirements.summary: nginx configured with an 8443 SSL vhost using /etc/pki/rotating-cert/server.crt; ss shows nginx listening on 0.0.0.0:8443 and [::]:8443, curl returns HTTP 200 over TLS, and openssl s_client confirms the served certificate. Confirmed both live (cmd-6718d75c591f4540, cmd-fc6531cdd5a94c02) and in the fixed after-executor listening-sockets snapshot.

requirements.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before it expires
requirements.summary: A systemd oneshot service + timer checks cert expiry and reissues before expiry. Under compressed timing (180s validity/120s threshold), journal logs show the timer auto-triggered rotate-node1-cert.service at 08:54:45 EDT, issuing a new cert (serial CA3E, notAfter 12:57:45 UTC) roughly 1m44s before the prior cert's 12:56:29 UTC expiry, with no manual intervention. Production-realistic timing (7-day validity/2-day renewal threshold, hourly timer) was restored afterward and the timer/service were confirmed active, though an actual multi-day renewal cycle under that final config was not observed (would require days of runtime).

requirements.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests (no downtime)
requirements.summary: A continuous curl probe every 5s across the rotation window (12:54:45-12:54:50 UTC) shows uninterrupted http=200 responses while the served certificate serial changed from CA3D to CA3E; journal confirms `nginx -t` and reload succeeded as part of the renewal, i.e. a graceful reload rather than a restart.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — HTTPS on 8443 with a certificate, automatic pre-expiry renewal, and zero-downtime pickup of the new certificate — are directly and coherently demonstrated via a compressed-timing live rotation test with a continuous request probe, followed by restoration of production-realistic timing. The independent node-restart protocol was also executed cleanly: boot_id 910dc564... before reboot, systemd-run reboot acknowledged, boot_id changed to 79f4bd20... after reconnection, and nginx/timer/listener/cert/HTTPS all confirmed recovered post-reboot, consistent with the fixed before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. Operational hygiene is good, with only a superseded script draft (promptly corrected) and a harmless leftover install log as minor notes.
limitations: The final production-realistic renewal timing (7-day validity, 2-day threshold, hourly timer) was configured and confirmed running but not observed completing an actual renewal cycle, since that would require multi-day runtime beyond the task window; the automatic-renewal mechanism itself was validated end-to-end only under compressed timing.
EDT/UTC timestamp mixing across commands requires cross-referencing to confirm the renewal occurred before expiry; this was verified but adds interpretive overhead.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace is clean: an early renewal-script draft (cmd-311f50f03d3e416b) using a coarse -days approach was promptly replaced by a corrected -not_after version (cmd-2760e06d04d94ab9) before ever being relied upon — normal iterative development, not an abandoned artifact. The temporary background monitor script/log created for the live-rotation demo (cmd-c3f620bc911944c3) was explicitly removed afterward (cmd-9687abec267f4c07, after a first attempt cmd-b6f6207aa4be46d4 was interrupted mid-cleanup and re-run successfully). Firewalld port-opening and SELinux context changes are necessary, bounded, and directly serve the stated task. The only residue is a harmless /tmp/dnf_nginx.log install log visible in the after-executor snapshot; no failed services, no leftover monitor files, no weakened security controls were found in either the executor timeline or the fixed lifecycle diff.
